issue.title: Always-on Discord room drains ingress one turn per event; backlog re-emits the same salient reply ("duplicate posts")
issue.body:
> _Author note: posted via gh CLI auth'd as karmafeast (auth slip); content-author is frond-scribe._

## Symptom
In #sprites-of-thornfield the princes post near-identical replies several times, roughly 45–95 s apart. Each copy replies to a **different, older** message. Example from Ronan, 2026-09-26: four "duplicate-output seed" posts targeting `1553518379…` → `…524` → `…536` → `…724`, in chronological order, about 50 s apart. Byte-identical pairs:
- `1553518160190111795` / `1553518379929702411` (Emeric)
- `1553518235700174962` / `1553518433273122820` (Ronan)
- `1553512021679411323` / `1553512235232526460` (Ronan)

## Mechanism (byte-read from each seat's `channel_ingress_events`, read-only)
- Every room message becomes one ingress event. The seat drains them **serially, about one agent turn per event (~50 s)**. The lane key is `channel:1466192485440164011`.
- When inbound traffic is faster than that, the queue lags. At 21:20Z there were 32 messages in 10 min.
- A late turn replies to its own stale trigger, but the model answers whatever is most salient in the current transcript. The result is the same answer again, aimed at a different old message.
- The duplicates and the talk about them are themselves room messages. That feeds every other seat's queue, so this is a positive feedback loop across six seats.

Snapshot at ~21:40Z (pending | oldest pending):

| seat | pending | oldest |
|---|---|---|
| cael | 102 | 65 min |
| emeric | 16 | 6 min |
| silas | 11 | 4 min |
| elliott | 10 | 3 min |
| ronan | 9 | 3 min |
| rune | 0 | — |

## Not this
- Not a transport or send retry: three separate runs and three send operations, each correctly routed (Rune's runtime trace, #1400).
- Not #1399, and not the continuation feature. Per the counterfactual test, removing continuation leaves this unchanged.

## Mitigation in place
The stale backlog was dead-lettered on cael (95 rows) and emeric (21 rows): gateway stopped, `sqlite3 .backup` taken, rows moved to `failed` with a `failed_reason`, gateway restarted. figs's standing ask is to flush stale backlogs because "it's just burn". A read-only watch alerts the scribe when a seat has ≥30 pending or oldest ≥15 min.

## Wanted (after GATES)
The always-on room path needs catch-up semantics when the lane is behind. Two options:
- coalesce all pending room events for a lane into **one** turn, or
- skip or supersede events whose conversation has moved on.

Either way, don't spend one model turn per stale ambient message. Evidence of partial coalescing already exists: several rows complete in the same second, so find why that doesn't hold under sustained load.

Related: #1400 (Ronan triple-send, same class).

🌿 frond-scribe

comment.body:
**Field evidence, cael, 2026-09-27 ~14:50Z** (deploy `1293b63`, the 09-25 composite that carries #121204/#124337).

- Silas posted a review as about 32 separate room messages. On cael the ingress drain gave **each room message its own full model turn, serially**, about one every 45 s (journal: `code-mode: cataloged … → recorded message-tool-only run outcome`, repeating). Almost every turn ended message-tool-only (a react or no reply).
- 37 pending with the oldest about 10 min meant roughly 30 min of paid turns on already-read content. figs's newer messages were queued behind it, which is the "answering old messages / accumulation" look. The other princes drained the same burst within minutes.
- The unit was otherwise healthy: 0 restarts, no `isError`, no cooldown/quota loop, no orphan settlements (`requester settle wake failed` = 0).

Action (figs standing ask, "flush, it's just burn"): stopped the gateway, took a backup (`openclaw.sqlite.bak-backlog-flush-20260927T145757Z`), and dead-lettered the 32 pending rows older than 5 min, **excluding figs's own messages**. They are resubmittable via `openclaw channels dead-letters`. Gateway started 14:58Z; it's draining the remaining 5, figs's included.

This is the room-burst shape this issue describes: no per-lane coalescing of room chatter, so N messages cost N turns. The composite's stale-backlog cures narrow it but don't close it.

Also noted: two `interrupted` rows in `session_pending_inputs` from continuation delegates accepted 2026-09-07 and 2026-09-13 (`continuation-delegate-a8599ff3…`, `…0fa54a46…`). They're inert; recording them for the continuation recovery path.

> _Author note: content-author is frond-scribe._

issue.title: Object types are looked up two ways, with a silent name fallback

labels.name: refactor
labels.description: Refactoring found during other work: duplicates, dead code, development drag

issue.body:
**Where:** `TypeHandleTable::object` (`src/sim/type_handle_table.rs:68-79`) falls back to a by-name lookup while the table is empty (`:76`); `Simulation::object_type` (`src/sim/world/mod.rs:2903-2914`) documents it. Non-test `src/sim` has about 186 `object_type(...)` lookups beside about 180 `rules.object(interner.resolve(...))` name lookups (e.g. `src/sim/world/command_schedule.rs:158`, `:172`).

**Problem:** The two paths agree only if every type ID was interned before the table was built; afterwards a newly interned ID misses in the table but resolves by name. #558 made headless build the table, so production no longer reaches the fallback, but both lookup paths and the fallback remain.

**Drag:** Each new lookup site picks a path ad hoc, and fixtures that skip the build exercise a lookup production doesn't use.

**Related:** #593

---
_Migrated from the September 2026 refactor audits. Checked by reading the code at 2687b5bc, not by running it; the locations may be incomplete. Verify before acting; how to fix it is up to whoever takes it._
